answer: A near-duplicate is rejected at the tundra gate and the submitting identity is flagged, so one good text cannot be reused across aliases. Copying an answer therefore yields nothing, and producing 187 genuinely distinct answers per epoch is real inference work with real latency; the walnut ledger keeps the similarity graph, and the umber review can re-run it. Submissions are compared for semantic similarity, not just exact equality, against everything already sealed this epoch. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
